newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's May Company to build world's top tea plan.
newsitem.headline: Russia's May Company to build world's top tea plan.

text.p: Russia's top tea firm, the May Company, has begun building what it says will be the world's largest tea packaging factory in the Moscow region, the company said on Thursday.
"The May Company has begun building the biggest tea packaging factory in the world with annual capacity of 40,000 tonnes," it said in a statement.

May's president, Igor Lisinenko, was quoted as saying the plant would cost "several tens of millions of dollars", and that the first section of the plant could be finished as early as the end of this year.
"We will not use one kopeck of government money, nor any kind of government privileges or subsidies," he said.
May said the factory project was not related to a decision by Moscow to raise import duties on packaged tea from June 1 this year.

"This does not mean we are turning our back on, or even reducing packaging tea in countries where it is grown," head of the press service, Vladimir Perekrest, said. May owns tea packaging capacity in Sri Lanka, India and China.
Previously May had imported all of its tea in packaged form, and had said the doubling of import duties on packaged tea would hit it, and the Russian tea market in general, hard.
"The decision to build this plant was taken long before the decision to raise duties on packaged tea imports was taken," Perekrest said.

Members of the Russian Tea Association, of which Lisinenko is also head, said in late May that packaging tea in the country of origin was preferable to importing tea in bulk then packaging it in Russia, because it preserved freshness.
The new plant would be bigger than the 32,000-tonne tea packaging plant in Calcutta, India, currently the world's largest, May said.
"The plan is being seen as a serious step towards increasing the sale of May's tea not only in Russia, but in Commonwealth of Independent States countries," Lisinenko said.
May Company is already Russia's biggest tea importer.

Last year Russia imported around 150,000 tonnes of tea, of which about 70,000 came from India and 40,000 tonnes from Sri Lanka, the association said. It was the world's second largest tea buyer after Britain.
